summary.headline: Fortis Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR 2,735 crore, with operating EBITDA pre-ESOP up 19.2% to INR 663 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 2,735 crore in Q2 FY27, up 17.3% YoY, driven by the hospital business (up 18.6% to INR 2,340 crore). Operating EBITDA pre-ESOP was INR 663 crore at a 24.2% margin, up from 23.9%. Diagnostics (Agilus) grew more slowly at 12.2% on gross revenue, and management said it expects 12-13% growth for FY27. Management declined to guide FY28 margins, citing drug price capping on 137 oncology drugs, and guided FY27 post-ESOP margin to be flat at around 22%.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,340 crore (+18.6%) and H1 INR 4,527 crore (+18.8%). Occupancy 72% (vs 71%), occupied beds 3,616 (+9%), ARPP INR 2.1 lakh (+6.8%). Renal, neuro and orthopaedics grew 27%, 28% and 30%.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 448 crore (+12.2%); H1 INR 855 crore (+11.2%). Tests processed 11.39 million (+7.2%); patient volume +5.8% YoY. B2C:B2B mix 54:46; wellness revenue +28%, specialised testing +14%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 190 crore (+12.4%), about 8% of Q2 revenue, flat share versus Q2 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to be flattish at around 22% post-ESOP, in line with FY26 (management confirmed post-ESOP basis).
No FY28 margin guidance given; management cited drug price capping circular (137 oncology drugs, effective November) as a negative for profitability, with impact not yet quantifiable.
FY29 25% margin guidance still stands if no drug-cap impact, per Vivek Goyal.
Diagnostics FY27 revenue growth expected at 12-13%; mid-teens growth in a few quarters, then industry growth.
FY27 ESOP expense expected around INR 140 crore.
capex_capacity: Committed capex about INR 3,500 crore over the next 3-3.5 years for brownfield and acquired beds.
Around 600 beds to be added in FY27 (about 100 from Suguna acquisition, rest brownfield at FMRI, Noida, Faridabad, Manesar); around 200 beds per year of brownfield for the next two years.
Mohali and Shalimar Bagh brownfield expansions targeted for completion by FY30; Punjab (Amritsar, Mohali) adds about 500+ beds, with occupancy above 70% and capacity constrained.
Suguna Hospital (Bengaluru): acquired for INR 270 crore incl. land, building and stamp duty; a further about INR 140 crore for 40 more beds and renovation; 110 beds, potential 150.
FMRI new block ready, awaiting final approvals expected within the month; Manesar radiation oncology expected by Feb (Q4 CY).

400-bed greenfield super specialty hospital in Ashok Vihar, New Delhi via long-term services agreement, about four years out; further greenfield projects not included in the 2,000-bed figure, which is about three to four years of visibility.
Diagnostics: Genexus systems being deployed for next-generation sequencing and molecular diagnostics; 4,551 customer touch points at 30 Sep 2026.
demand_pricing: IP volume growth about 13% YoY; ARPP growth of 6.8% driven mainly by case mix (robotics, complex cases), with price contributing about 1.5 percentage points.
Occupancy below 70% in Bengaluru cluster (Bannerghatta Road about 58%); Punjab units above 70%, some above 75%.
Digital revenue +18.6% to 29.5% of hospital revenue; 15 hospitals above 20% EBITDA margin, accounting for 84% of hospital revenue (vs 13 hospitals, 76%).
Around 300 doctors added QoQ; FMRI has no major attrition, with new clinical hires in head and neck, rheumatology and neurology.
Gleneagles O&M (Hyderabad, Chennai) operations almost flat in the first year, with improvement expected next year.
Drug-price capping: oncology drugs about one-third of oncology revenue; impact not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Punjab and Mumbai growing slower, and is Fortis lagging listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Punjab is capacity-constrained, with about 500+ beds coming from Amritsar and Mohali expansions; other clusters are growing fast. He declined to compare with competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bangalore occupancy low and why buy a small 110-bed hospital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small community hospitals complement larger flagships in a cluster. Bannerghatta Road is about 58% occupied, and TMI Yeshwanthpur is still ramping up. Suguna was bought via direct negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the 2,000 beds and the committed capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the 2,000 beds are completed acquisitions and brownfield expansions, excluding Gleneagles and the 400-bed Delhi greenfield. Committed capex is about INR 3,500 crore over 3-3.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What returns hurdle does Fortis apply to acquisitions, and how is capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Board-approved benchmark is IRR of at least 15% and payback within 8-10 years, though strategic factors can override. IHH may take its stake above 50%, which could bring about INR 10,000 crore at current prices; management says capital is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins and guidance be revised given drug-price capping?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said FY27 margin should be flattish at about 22% post-ESOP, with no FY28 guidance until the impact of the drug circular is clear. He reaffirmed that FY29 25% guidance holds if there is no impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for diagnostics growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vijender Singh said FY27 growth is expected at 12-13%, with mid-teens growth in a few quarters, then industry growth. Brand transition impact is largely behind them.

risks_watch: Drug-price capping on 137 oncology drugs (circular effective November): profitability impact not yet quantified; management says oncology drugs are about one-third of oncology revenue.
Forensic audit ordered by court is ongoing; management expects completion within about six months of appointment.
Ramp-up drag from Manesar, People Tree and Bengaluru occupancy; FMRI new block approvals pending.
Diagnostics volume growth (5.3% H1 tests) lags peers; management targets improvement.
Rising debt: net debt INR 2,188 crore, with heavy debt expected this fiscal year; repayment in about two years in a steady state.
Gleneagles O&M contract flat operationally in year one.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, network expansion and cluster strategy, but cautious and non-committal on forward margins and drug-price impact, declining to quantify FY28 margins.
key_quotes: So, our margin guidance more or less remains intact, though the challenges which we highlighted in the last call remain.
So, we expect end of the current financial year, the EBITDA margin should be flattish, and future financial year, we would not like to comment on the margin in the present circumstances.
I think capital is not a constraint here. I think the constraint is getting the right opportunity at the right price.
Once this thing settles, we will be able to see how much we will be able to recover, how much we will not be able to do that.
